STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white, flat-centred plate with a raised rim band and no inner wall visible. This is a flat plate, roughly square with rounded corners.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: square/rounded-square dinner plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks like a medium-large dinner plate, so about 25 cm.
b) Reference cue: the lemon wedges are about 5-6 cm long. The plate spans roughly 4.5 to 5 lemon lengths across its width, giving about 25-28 cm.
Reconciled width: about 26 cm (square-ish, so area ≈ 26² ≈ 676 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items (plate, so footprint × thickness × density):
- Chopped greens (raw leafy/salad mix, dressed): covers about 25% of the plate area, roughly 170 cm². Mound about 2 cm thick at peak, average ~1 cm. Volume ≈ 170 ml; with dressing, ~0.4 g/ml effective. Estimate ≈ 60 g.
- Fish pieces (three or four pale fillet-like pieces with herb crust): about 60 cm² footprint, average thickness ~1.5 cm, volume ≈ 90 ml, density 1.0. Estimate ≈ 90 g.
- Cauliflower florets (steamed/roasted): about 110 cm² footprint, average ~1.5 cm, volume ≈ 165 ml, density 0.6. Estimate ≈ 100 g.
- Lemon wedges (4-5 wedges, mostly rind and pulp): about 50 cm² total, thin, volume ≈ 60 ml, density 0.6. Estimate ≈ 35 g.
- Red pepper/radish and bean-like garnish scattered through the salad: about 15 g.
- Olive oil/dressing visible on greens and fish: about 8 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No rice or grain base is visible; the plate is a single layer, so no hidden base beyond the greens and fish.

STEP 5 - Energy values (as served):
- Salad greens with dressing: ~60 kcal/100 g (dressing adds fat, leafy base ~25 kcal/100 g, so blended ~50).
- Fish with herb crust: ~150 kcal/100 g.
- Cauliflower, cooked with oil: ~50 kcal/100 g.
- Lemon: ~30 kcal/100 g.
- Garnish vegetables: ~30 kcal/100 g.
- Dressing/oil: ~850 kcal/100 g.

Totals: greens 60 g ≈ 30 kcal; fish 90 g ≈ 135 kcal; cauliflower 100 g ≈ 50 kcal; lemon 35 g ≈ 10 kcal; garnish 15 g ≈ 5 kcal; oil 8 g ≈ 68 kcal. Whole meal ≈ 300 kcal, about 310 g total.
